hero.title: About LeClap
hero.tagline: LeClap turns a JSON template and your own footage into a finished video. FFmpeg renders it in a terminal, a browser tab or on a phone: no model samples a single frame, and your footage is never uploaded.

cta.prompt: Ready to compose your first video?

story.title: From a Node library to every screen
story.lead: LeClap began as an npm package that compiles a JSON template into FFmpeg commands. It still does exactly that; everything since has been about running that one step in more places.

origin.title: A template in, a video out
origin.body: The first release of ffmpeg-video-composer: a Node library that reads a JSON template, compiles it into FFmpeg commands and runs them.

everywhere.title: The same template on every screen
everywhere.body: The engine gains a browser entry, with FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly, and a React Native one, with FFmpeg compiled into the app. The CLI and the MCP server ship the same day, as packages of their own.

now.title: One name for all of it
now.body: LeClap is the studio in this browser, the React Native app, the CLI and the MCP server. The engine still ships on npm under its first, admirably literal name: ffmpeg-video-composer.

author.name: Alexandre Mogère
author.bio: Paris-based software engineer building tools that empower creators, and writing about coding & AI at Zazen Code.

thanks.lead: None of this renders without FFmpeg.
thanks.body: Every clip, filter, and transition LeClap produces runs on FFmpeg — decades of open-source multimedia engineering kept alive by a worldwide community of volunteers.
